entries.effect: the verdict, the domain, the code and the description are what the newest Security answers for a name that does not match, an untrusted root and an expired certificate; a language in which the release names none of the three reasons gets the not trusted error
entries.reason: a departure from 12.0 in what the error says: the reason is read from the four strings the release gives for a failed evaluation in English, and the index of the certificate in the underlying error is a guess for a chain longer than one
entries.source: Security of iOS 12.0 arm64, _SecTrustEvaluateWithError at 0x181bffe78, which evaluates and answers YES for the results unspecified and proceed; the host's Security for the errors; an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 for what the release reports
the host's Security, where it answers the public key of the certificate; the release's own SecCertificateCopyPublicKey answers the same
the host's Security, where it answers the content of the DER integer of the serial number, its leading zero kept; read from the certificate's own encoding here

entries.reason: the text is English whatever the language of the device; iOS 12 also answers in the language of the device from the tables of its Security bundle, which iOS 6 does not have
entries.source: Security of iOS 12.0 arm64, _SecCopyErrorMessageString at 0x181bb6fa4 (the tables SecErrorMessages and SecDebugErrorMessages by the key of the status, then the text OSStatus followed by the number), the English table read from the Security bundle of 16.0, the host's own function through the differential run of tests/backports/host/errmsg, and an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 through tests/backports/device/secmessage12.m

entries.effect: errSecSuccess and the timestamps are NOT consulted: 6.1.3 has no certificate transparency at all, so a caller stapling timestamps gets no additional scrutiny and no error, and a chain that should only verify with CT verifies here
entries.reason: 6.1.3 has no SCT parser, no place in an evaluation where a timestamp is consulted, and no call that reads a stapled SCT back; the declared release is 12.1.1 per SecTrust.h:628, and first-rung answers 9.0 only because the held ladder has no cache between 12.0 and 16.0
entries.source: the armv7 shared caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3 through tools/cache-index (first-rung.py --rungs), which carry _SecTrustEvaluate, _SecTrustGetCertificateCount, _SecTrustGetCertificateAtIndex, _SecPolicyCreateBasicX509 and _SecPolicyCreateSSL and none of the fourteen names

entries.effect: the CFString "persistref", the same value this name and its misspelled twin both carry: dlsym off the host's own framework hands back the same string for each, which is how SecItem.h:553-556 declares them. 6.1.3 ignores the attribute - the string is in no held rung below 11.0 - so the port declares the key so a caller that passes it compiles
entries.reason: the attribute arrived in iOS 11; on this release no code reads it, so the port carries the key with the value the release itself would hand a caller
entries.source: the armv7 shared caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3 through tools/cache-index (first-rung.py --rungs), which carry _SecTrustEvaluate, _SecTrustGetCertificateCount, _SecTrustGetCertificateAtIndex, _SecPolicyCreateBasicX509 and _SecPolicyCreateSSL and none of the fourteen names; the value read by dlsym off the host framework, this Mac's own Security.framework, asked through the case in tests/backports/host/security/trust-accessors.m

entries.effect: the CFString "persistref", which is what the host's own Security.framework exports for this name - and 6.1.3 ignores the attribute: the string is in no held rung below 11.0, read out of all fifty per-release indexes, so no code path in the release compares a query against it. A caller that adds an item with this attribute and later queries by it gets no match, while the item is still findable by its other attributes
entries.reason: the attribute arrived in iOS 11 with the name the framework still exports; on this release there is no code that reads it, so the port declares the key so a caller that passes it compiles and passes the release's own string
